words.definition: the process of copying DNA before cell division
words.example: DNA replication produces two DNA molecules from one original molecule.

words.definition: DNA replication in which each daughter molecule contains one original strand and one newly synthesized strand
words.example: Semi-conservative replication preserves one parental DNA strand in each copy.

words.definition: an existing nucleic-acid strand used to determine the sequence of a new complementary strand
words.example: Each parental DNA strand acts as a template strand during replication.

words.definition: the specific matching of molecular partners, especially bases that pair according to base-pairing rules
words.example: Base complementarity allows accurate DNA copying.

words.definition: an enzyme that separates the two strands of DNA by disrupting hydrogen bonds between bases
words.example: Helicase opens the DNA double helix during replication.

words.definition: an enzyme that synthesizes DNA by adding nucleotides complementary to a template strand
words.example: DNA polymerase extends a new DNA strand in the 5′ to 3′ direction.

words.definition: a laboratory technique that rapidly amplifies a selected DNA region through repeated cycles
words.japanese: ポリメラーゼ連鎖反応（PCR）
words.example: Polymerase chain reaction can produce millions of copies of a DNA target.

words.definition: a short DNA sequence that binds to a target and provides a starting point for DNA synthesis in PCR
words.example: PCR primers determine which DNA region is amplified.

words.definition: a machine that repeatedly changes temperature to carry out PCR cycles
words.example: A thermal cycler automates denaturation, annealing and extension steps.

words.definition: a heat-stable DNA polymerase commonly used in PCR
words.example: Taq polymerase remains active after repeated high-temperature PCR cycles.

words.definition: the high-temperature PCR stage in which double-stranded DNA separates into single strands
words.example: During the denaturation step, hydrogen bonds between DNA strands are disrupted.

words.definition: the PCR stage in which primers bind to complementary sequences on single-stranded DNA
words.example: Annealing temperature affects how specifically PCR primers bind.

words.definition: the PCR stage in which DNA polymerase synthesizes new DNA from the primers
words.example: During extension, Taq polymerase adds complementary nucleotides.

words.definition: a technique that separates DNA fragments or other charged molecules by movement through a gel in an electric field
words.example: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments mainly according to size.

words.definition: analysis of variable DNA regions to compare biological samples or individuals
words.example: DNA profiling can compare samples from a crime scene and a suspect.

words.definition: a piece of DNA containing a limited number of nucleotides
words.example: Shorter DNA fragments usually move farther through an electrophoresis gel.

words.definition: production of many copies of a selected DNA sequence
words.example: PCR is widely used for DNA amplification.

words.definition: genetic comparison used to assess whether an individual could be a biological parent
words.example: Paternity testing compares inherited DNA markers between a child and possible father.

words.definition: scientific examination of evidence for legal or criminal cases
words.example: DNA profiling is often used in forensic investigation.

words.definition: an identifiable DNA sequence or variation used to track inheritance or distinguish samples
words.example: Variable DNA markers are useful in genetic identification.

words.definition: the synthesis of RNA using a DNA template
words.example: During transcription, a gene's DNA sequence is copied into RNA.

words.definition: an enzyme that synthesizes RNA from a DNA template
words.example: RNA polymerase joins RNA nucleotides during transcription.

words.definition: mRNA, an RNA molecule that carries coding information from DNA to a ribosome
words.example: Messenger RNA is translated at ribosomes.

words.definition: tRNA, an RNA molecule that carries a specific amino acid and pairs its anticodon with an mRNA codon
words.example: Transfer RNA brings amino acids to the ribosome.

words.definition: rRNA, RNA that forms a major structural and catalytic component of ribosomes
words.example: Ribosomal RNA helps form the ribosome's functional core.

words.definition: the synthesis of a polypeptide using the codon sequence of mRNA
words.example: Translation converts nucleotide information into an amino-acid sequence.

words.definition: one of the two structural parts that combine to form a functional ribosome
words.japanese: リボソームサブユニット
words.example: Small and large ribosomal subunits assemble on mRNA during translation.

words.definition: a sequence of three nucleotides in mRNA that specifies an amino acid or stop signal
words.example: The codon AUG usually specifies methionine and can act as a start codon.

words.definition: a three-nucleotide sequence in tRNA complementary to an mRNA codon
words.example: A tRNA anticodon pairs with the appropriate mRNA codon.

words.definition: the property that most amino acids are specified by more than one codon
words.example: Genetic code degeneracy can make some base substitutions silent.

words.definition: the near-universal correspondence between codons and amino acids across organisms
words.example: The universal genetic code allows genes to function across many species.

words.definition: the assembly of amino acids into a polypeptide chain
words.example: Polypeptide synthesis occurs during translation.

words.definition: the formation of covalent bonds linking adjacent amino acids in a growing polypeptide
words.example: Ribosomes catalyse peptide bond formation.

words.definition: the use of information in a gene to produce a functional RNA or protein product
words.example: Different patterns of gene expression produce different cell functions.

words.definition: the organization of genetic information into groups of three nucleotides
words.example: The triplet code means three mRNA bases form one codon.

words.definition: the order of amino acids in a polypeptide
words.example: A gene's base sequence ultimately influences the amino acid sequence of a protein.

words.definition: a mutation affecting a single nucleotide position or a very small number of nucleotides
words.example: A point mutation can alter one codon in a gene.

words.definition: a change in the nucleotide sequence of a gene
words.example: A gene mutation can create a new allele.

words.definition: a mutation in which one nucleotide base is replaced by another
words.example: A base substitution may change one codon.

words.definition: a mutation caused by addition of one or more nucleotides to a DNA sequence
words.example: A one-base insertion can shift the reading frame.

words.definition: a mutation caused by removal of one or more nucleotides from a DNA sequence
words.example: Deletion of a nucleotide can alter all downstream codons.

words.definition: a common genetic variation involving a difference at one nucleotide position
words.example: Single-nucleotide polymorphisms can be used as genetic markers.

words.definition: a mutation that changes the reading frame of a coding sequence, usually through insertion or deletion not in multiples of three
words.japanese: フレームシフト突然変異
words.example: A frameshift mutation can alter many amino acids after the mutation site.

words.definition: a physical or chemical agent that increases mutation rate
words.example: Ultraviolet radiation can act as a mutagen.

words.definition: a mutation arising naturally without deliberate exposure to an external mutagen
words.example: DNA copying errors can produce spontaneous mutations.

words.definition: a mutation caused by exposure to an external mutagenic agent
words.example: Ionizing radiation can cause induced mutations.

words.definition: a mutation in a cell lineage that produces gametes and can therefore be inherited
words.japanese: 生殖細胞系列突然変異
words.example: A germline mutation may be passed to offspring.

words.definition: a mutation in a non-reproductive body cell that is generally not inherited by offspring
words.example: Somatic mutations can contribute to cancer development.

words.definition: genetic differences among individuals that can be passed to offspring
words.example: Heritable variation provides raw material for natural selection.

words.definition: a chemical substance that increases the frequency of DNA mutations
words.example: Some compounds in tobacco smoke act as chemical mutagens.

words.definition: radiation capable of damaging DNA and increasing mutation rate
words.example: Ultraviolet light is a form of mutagenic radiation.

words.definition: an incorrectly inserted, omitted or altered nucleotide produced during DNA copying
words.example: A DNA replication error that escapes repair can become a permanent mutation.
